meta.schwerpunkt: Investigate whether post-mission analysis is a gap in the harness — should a mission analysis phase be launched after each individual mission completes, before the next mission launches?

observations.fact: The current mission lifecycle has four governed phases: (1) BEFORE: MDMP Mission Analysis (decision #13) for plans, S2 intelligence prep (decision #26) at plan start. (2) DURING: Agent executes, produces AAR per delegation duty. (3) AFTER EACH MISSION: Ad-hoc — the S3 reads returns, spot-checks, sometimes updates the running estimate. No governed process. (4) AFTER ALL MISSIONS: Reconciliation (M14 finding — ad-hoc), AAR/debrief (decision #36 — session end), handoff (decision #52). The gap in question is phase 3.
observations.source: planning-brief.json decisions #13 (MDMP), #26 (S2 timing), #36 (Operational Learning), #4 (delegation duty); running-estimate.json:delegationLog (11 entries showing the S3 post-mission pattern)

observations.fact: In this session (5HyCwPtSDH), the S3 performed post-mission processing 11 times. The actual pattern was inconsistent: M1 returned inline (Explore failure) — S3 read output, wrote FRAGORD. M2 returned — S3 spot-checked AAR structure, converted format, wrote to scratch. M3 returned — S3 validated JSON, checked schema structure. M4 returned — S3 spot-checked .current-session race claim. M5 returned — S3 spot-checked skill count. M7 returned — S3 verified file count. M9 returned — S3 reported findings to commander. M11 returned — S3 reported findings. M12 returned — S3 reported findings. M14 returned — S3 reported findings. M16 returned — S3 reported findings. NO mission return triggered: assumption re-check, running estimate update, Schwerpunkt re-assessment, or FRAGORD for the next mission based on new findings.

In the 40-agent session (Z1IhGrcgGO), the commander directed ad-hoc post-mission analysis at three points. L2040: 'consolidate this prompt and our recent conversation into a single clarifying set of questions' — this was AFTER multiple investigations had returned. L2391: 'think hard using lots of tokens with everything you have in context about what I as the user should instruct you to do next' — this was a FULL situation assessment after accumulated agent returns. L3098-L3134: four-turn cascade where the commander demanded progressively deeper consolidated responses with reverse-chronological conversation audit. The S3 NEVER independently initiated any of these analysis steps.
observations.source: 40agent-human-messages.md L2040, L2391, L3098-L3134; m14-reconciliation-patterns-aar.json O-2 ('reconciliation was ALWAYS initiated by the commander, never by the S3 independently')

observations.fact: M11 (assumption propagation) found that 8 of the S3's 12 deviations were caused by unverified assumptions. Several of these assumptions could have been caught by a post-mission analysis step: after M1 returned showing Explore agents cannot write, the S3 should have checked whether the running estimate's assumption about agent types needed updating. After M4 returned showing concurrent sessions exist, the S3 should have checked whether earlier missions (M1-M3) were designed under the single-session assumption. Neither check happened because no governed step required it.
observations.source: m11-assumption-propagation-aar.json O-5 (12 deviations, 8 from unverified assumptions), O-6 (5 tracked assumptions, 12 untracked deviations)

observations.fact: M16 (3-depth verification trace) showed that a verified assumption in the running estimate was never challenged by subsequent missions. The 'N-level delegation depth of 3 is sufficient' assumption was marked verified before M11 and M12 launched. Both M11 and M12 noticed it but did not question the verification because it was already marked 'verified'. A post-mission analysis step that re-checked assumptions against new findings would have caught this: M11's discovery of the assumption taxonomy and M12's discovery of 17 unflagged assumptions both provided evidence that the verification standard was insufficient.
observations.source: m16-3depth-verification-trace.json timeline sequences 6-7 (M11 and M12 took 'verified' status at face value)

observations.fact: M14 (reconciliation patterns) found that the 40-agent session's four-turn reconciliation cascade (L3098-L3134) produced the most strategically valuable output of the entire 3-day session — including Lagebeurteilung, blast radius analysis, lifecycle transitions, and delegation duty expansions. This HIGH-VALUE output came from a POST-MISSION analysis step (synthesizing what agents had produced). M14 insight I-5: 'Reconciliation is where the highest-leverage governance decisions emerge.'

The planning brief decision #36 (Operational Learning) defines a 16-component pipeline. Component 12 specifies: 'execution completes -> S3 delegates to S2 -> S2 invokes /debrief -> AAR produced.' This pipeline is scoped to SESSION end or PLAN completion. It does NOT specify what happens between individual missions within a session. Decision #26 says S2 is spawned at 'plan start' and 'plan end' — not after each mission.

The running estimate has an 'assumptions' array (5 items at v4) and a 'findings' array (16 items). Neither was systematically updated after individual missions returned. Assumptions accumulated without re-verification. Findings were added when the S3 remembered to, not when a governed process required it. The running estimate version went from 1 to 4 across the session — updates happened at arbitrary points, not at mission boundaries.
observations.source: running-estimate.json version history (v1-v4 at irregular intervals), assumptions array (items added ad-hoc), findings array (16 items, not aligned to mission completion events)

observations.fact: Decision #50 (running estimate) says: 'continuously maintained state document for all plan executions, enforced by SessionStart hook + /delegate skill.' The word 'continuously' implies ongoing maintenance, but the enforcement mechanisms are at session boundaries (SessionStart hook) and delegation boundaries (/delegate skill). There is no enforcement mechanism at mission RETURN boundaries. The running estimate is supposed to be continuous but the governance has no trigger for 'mission just completed, update the estimate.'

The OODA loop (Boyd) specifies ORIENT after every OBSERVE. In the mission lifecycle: OBSERVE = the mission runs and produces output. ORIENT = analyze the output and update your mental model. DECIDE = determine the next action. ACT = launch the next mission. The harness governs ACT (delegation duty) but not ORIENT (post-mission analysis). The S3 goes directly from OBSERVE to ACT, skipping the explicit ORIENT step. The commander's ad-hoc interventions (L2040, L2391, L3098) were forced ORIENT phases.
observations.source: OODA loop doctrine (Boyd), m14-reconciliation-patterns-aar.json O-2 (commander always initiated reconciliation)

observations.fact: MDMP (US Army doctrine) Step 2 is Mission Analysis, which is PRE-PLAN. The equivalent post-operation step is the AAR (FM 7-0), which is post-OPERATION — not post-individual-mission. In the Bundeswehr doctrine, Lagebeurteilung is a periodic re-assessment with fixed categories, done at fixed intervals regardless of events. It is not event-triggered (not 'after each mission') but time-triggered (at regular intervals or transition points). Decision #36 component (9) already proposes a Stop hook for periodic AAR reminders — this is closer to Lagebeurteilung than to post-mission analysis.
observations.source: planning-brief.json meta.sourceFrameworks (MDMP Step 2), glossary.json Lagebeurteilung definition, decision #36 component (9) aar-reminder.sh

observations.fact: The Deming PDCA cycle has CHECK after DO. Toyota A3 has a follow-up step verifying the countermeasure worked. Both are post-ACTION checks. But critically, both are lightweight: PDCA Check is 'did the Do produce the expected result?' not 'full situation re-assessment.' A3 follow-up is 'did the metric move?' not 'revisit all assumptions.' The question is whether post-mission analysis should be a FULL Lagebeurteilung or a LIGHTWEIGHT check.
observations.source: s2c-framework-proposals.json FP-1 provenance (Deming PDCA), FP-2 context rot techniques

observations.fact: The session decision D-CONTEXT-ROT-HOOK proposes a Stop hook that fires at 20%+ context usage. Its content includes: 're-read running estimate, audit conversation in reverse chronological order, check for stale assumptions, surface discrepancies.' This is a PERIODIC Lagebeurteilung, not an event-driven post-mission analysis. The proposed PreToolUse hook on Agent tool (D-CONTEXT-ROT-HOOK component 9) fires BEFORE each delegation — 'reminding S3 to refresh running estimate and verify delegation premise.' This is pre-NEXT-mission, not post-THIS-mission. Neither hook covers the gap: what happens BETWEEN mission return and next delegation.

This session's M9 AAR found that the S3 treated missions as 'independent work units, not as intelligence feeds.' M9 insight I-3: 'The S3 launched a batch and planned to reconcile later — treating subagent output as deliverables rather than intelligence.' This is the behavioral symptom of the missing post-mission analysis step: without a governed ORIENT phase, the S3 defaults to a collect-then-reconcile pattern rather than an analyze-as-you-go pattern.

In the 40-agent session, the commander said (L1830): 'you are smart enough to figure out by loading the entire large briefing into context and auditing our recent conversations from the last 3 days.' This is the commander directing a mid-session situation assessment — a Lagebeurteilung triggered by the commander's observation that the S3 was not connecting findings to the broader context. The S3 had completed several missions but had not synthesized their outputs into an updated picture.

insights.analysis: THE MISSION LIFECYCLE HAS A GOVERNED GAP BETWEEN MISSION RETURN AND NEXT DELEGATION. The harness governs: delegation (duty, 9-13 components), execution (agent runs), session-end processing (AAR, harvest, archive, handoff). It does NOT govern what happens when an individual mission returns. Decision #26 says S2 at 'plan start' and 'plan end.' Decision #36 says AAR at 'execution completes.' Decision #50 says 'continuously maintained' but enforcement is at session/delegation boundaries. The gap: no decision, rule, skill, hook, or reference specifies what the S3 MUST DO when a mission returns before launching the next one.

THE COMMANDER IS THE ONLY POST-MISSION ANALYSIS MECHANISM, AND IT DOES NOT SCALE. In both sessions, the S3 never independently performed post-mission analysis beyond reading the return output and spot-checking. Every substantive analysis of mission returns was commander-initiated (L2040, L2391, L3098-L3134 in the 40-agent session; the reconciliation mission Schwerpunkt in this session). The S3's default behavior is: read return, report to commander, wait for next instruction. Without the commander's ORIENT interventions, findings accumulate without synthesis, assumptions go unchecked, and the running estimate drifts from reality.

POST-MISSION ANALYSIS WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ASSUMPTION PROPAGATION EARLIER. M11 found 8 deviations caused by unverified assumptions. M16 found a 'verified' assumption that was never challenged. A lightweight post-mission check — 'did this mission's findings invalidate any assumptions in the running estimate?' — would have been a structural catch mechanism. When M4 returned showing concurrent sessions are real, a post-mission check would have triggered: 'ASSUMPTION INVALIDATED: M1-M3 designed under single-session assumption. Running estimate updated. Next mission adjusted.' Instead, the discovery was noted but not connected to earlier missions.

POST-MISSION ANALYSIS IS THE ORIENT PHASE OF OODA — AND IT IS WHERE HIGH-LEVERAGE GOVERNANCE DECISIONS EMERGE. The 40-agent session's reconciliation cascade produced Lagebeurteilung, blast radius, and lifecycle transitions. This session's reconciliation produced 10 ranked proposal themes from 38 proposals. Both instances show that analyzing mission outputs — not just collecting them — produces strategically valuable synthesis. The OODA ORIENT phase is not optional overhead; it is where the agent updates its mental model. Skipping it means the S3 operates on a stale mental model with each successive mission.

THE CORRECT MECHANISM IS A LIGHTWEIGHT CHECK, NOT A FULL LAGEBEURTEILUNG. Military doctrine distinguishes periodic situation assessments (Lagebeurteilung — fixed intervals, mandatory categories, even if nothing changed) from event-triggered checks (battle update assessments — triggered by specific events, scoped to what changed). PDCA Check is 'did it work?' not 'reassess everything.' The post-mission step should be an event-triggered MINI-CHECK scoped to what this mission changed, not a full Lagebeurteilung that reviews everything. A full Lagebeurteilung after every mission would be overkill for simple missions (M6 trash search) and appropriate only at major transition points.

THE CHECK INTENSITY SHOULD SCALE WITH MISSION IMPACT. This session's missions varied from trivial (M6: check Trash, 1 file) to high-impact (M4: concurrent session architecture, 5 proposals, design changes). A post-mission check for M6 should take seconds: 'Files not in Trash, no new findings, no assumptions invalidated, carry on.' A post-mission check for M4 should take minutes: 'Concurrent sessions exist, ASSUMPTION INVALIDATED: single session per repo. M1-M3 may need adjustment. Running estimate updated with 5 new findings. Schwerpunkt unchanged.' The check is proportional to what the mission produced.

THE PRE-DELEGATION HOOK (D-CONTEXT-ROT-HOOK COMPONENT 9) IS CLOSE BUT ON THE WRONG SIDE OF THE BOUNDARY. The proposed PreToolUse hook on Agent says 'refresh running estimate and verify delegation premise before each launch.' This fires BEFORE the next delegation. But the analysis of the previous mission's output should happen AFTER the return, not before the next launch. If the S3 launches M5 immediately after M4 returns, then reads M4's output for the pre-M6 hook check, M5 was launched without the benefit of M4's findings. The check needs to be post-RETURN, not pre-NEXT-LAUNCH. In practice, these are often the same moment — but the conceptual boundary matters because it determines the trigger.

proposals.what: Add a POST-MISSION CHECK (Nachbesprechung) as a governed lightweight step between mission return and next delegation. The check is a 4-question protocol, NOT a full Lagebeurteilung, NOT a subagent launch, NOT a mandatory delay. It is an inline S3 mental checklist that takes seconds for trivial missions and minutes for impactful ones.

protocol.name: Nachbesprechung (post-mission check)
protocol.trigger: Every time a delegated mission returns output to the S3
questions: Q1: ASSUMPTIONS — Did this mission's findings invalidate any assumption in the running estimate? If yes: update status to 'falsified', add the finding as evidence.
Q2: SCHWERPUNKT — Does this mission's output change the session Schwerpunkt or the next mission's premise? If yes: consider FRAGORD for already-running missions.
Q3: RUNNING ESTIMATE — What facts, findings, or decisions from this mission need to be added to the running estimate RIGHT NOW (not deferred to session end)?
Q4: NEXT MISSION — Should the next planned mission be adjusted based on what this one found? Changed scope, different angle, added verification?
protocol.scalingHeuristic: If the mission produced 0 findings and 0 proposals (trivial): Q1-Q4 are a 10-second mental scan. If the mission produced findings or proposals: Q1-Q4 require actually reading the output and connecting to the running estimate. If the mission produced design-changing findings (new architecture, invalidated assumptions): Q1-Q4 require running estimate update before proceeding.
protocol.output: No formal output artifact. The running estimate is updated if Q1-Q3 require it. The next delegation prompt reflects Q4 if applicable. The check is INLINE — the S3 thinks, does not delegate.

proposals.why: This fills the governed gap between mission return and next delegation. The 4 questions encode exactly what the commander was doing ad-hoc: checking assumptions (L2391 scope-creep analysis), checking Schwerpunkt alignment (L3098 'what did we miss?'), updating state (L1830 'load the briefing and audit'), and adjusting next steps (L2070 'update the briefing with AAR findings'). The commander's ad-hoc interventions formalize into a 4-question checklist.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Cost: seconds per trivial mission, minutes per impactful mission. 11 missions in this session would add ~20 minutes total. Benefit: M4's concurrent-session finding would have triggered M1-M3 premise re-check. M11's assumption taxonomy would have triggered running estimate assumption re-classification. M16's finding about verification quality would have been caught by Q1 ('did this invalidate the verified assumption?'). Risk: over-application — the S3 performs a full situation assessment after every trivial mission. Mitigation: the scaling heuristic explicitly says 0-finding missions get a 10-second scan.

proposals.what: Make the Nachbesprechung part of the delegation duty rather than a separate governed phase. Add it as delegation duty component 13 (or whatever the next available number is after the assumptions block and operational learning duty): 'After the delegated agent returns, before delegating the next mission, perform the 4-question post-mission check (Nachbesprechung). Update the running estimate if Q1-Q3 require it. Adjust the next mission if Q4 requires it.'
proposals.why: The delegation duty already governs the full delegation lifecycle: components 1-9 govern the LAUNCH, component 10 (proposed) governs PATTERN-CHECK before launch, component 11 (proposed) governs ASSUMPTIONS injection, component 12 (proposed) governs OPERATIONAL LEARNING injection. Adding the post-mission check as a component makes the delegation duty cover the COMPLETE lifecycle: prepare (1-12) -> launch -> return -> check (13) -> prepare next (1-12). The delegation duty becomes a full OODA loop: ACT (launch) -> OBSERVE (mission runs) -> ORIENT (Nachbesprechung) -> DECIDE (prepare next delegation).
proposals.barrier_analysis: This extends the delegation duty from 12 proposed components to 13. The duty is becoming long. However: components 1-12 fire BEFORE delegation. Component 13 fires AFTER return. The two halves are temporally separated. The S3 does not need to hold all 13 in mind simultaneously — it needs 1-12 at launch time and 13 at return time. The Nachbesprechung is the simplest component: 4 yes/no questions. It adds less cognitive load than the assumptions block (component 11) or the operational learning duty (component 12).

proposals.what: Define the Nachbesprechung as distinct from three related but different concepts: (1) RECONCILIATION (M14) — synthesis of MULTIPLE parallel mission outputs. Nachbesprechung is per-SINGLE-mission. (2) LAGEBEURTEILUNG — periodic full situation assessment at transition points. Nachbesprechung is event-triggered and scoped to one mission. (3) AAR/DEBRIEF (decision #36) — structured learning artifact at session/plan end. Nachbesprechung produces no formal artifact — it is an inline mental check. (4) S2 CONSOLIDATION (decision #26) — S2 agent reading channel and cross-referencing at plan end. Nachbesprechung is the S3 doing a quick check, not launching an S2.
proposals.why: The harness already has 4 analysis concepts at different scopes. Adding a 5th requires clear differentiation to avoid the term collision problem (M12 AM-6: 'finding' used in 3 incompatible senses). Nachbesprechung is specifically: per-mission, event-triggered, inline, lightweight, no formal output, 4 questions. It occupies the unique space of 'after each individual mission, before the next' that none of the other 4 concepts cover.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Adding a 5th analysis concept increases complexity. Mitigation: the 5 concepts form a clean hierarchy by scope. Nachbesprechung (per-mission) < Reconciliation (per-batch of parallel missions) < Lagebeurteilung (periodic session-level) < AAR (session/plan end) < S2 Consolidation (cross-session). Each triggers at a different boundary. The vocabulary exists to distinguish them. Filing 'Nachbesprechung' via /glossary skill would be appropriate.

proposals.what: Reframe the proposed PreToolUse hook on Agent (D-CONTEXT-ROT-HOOK component 9) as a POST-RETURN check rather than a PRE-LAUNCH check. Instead of 'before launching the next agent, refresh the running estimate,' make it 'when a mission returns, perform the Nachbesprechung before proceeding.' This could be a Stop hook (fires after S3 turns) or a SubagentCompleted hook (if Claude Code adds such an event). In the absence of a SubagentCompleted event, the behavioral instruction in the delegation duty (P-2) is the only mechanism.
proposals.why: The conceptual boundary matters: the check analyzes what just CAME BACK, not what is about to GO OUT. A pre-launch hook may fire too late if the S3 has already composed the next delegation prompt before the hook triggers. A post-return check ensures the S3 processes the return BEFORE context-switching to the next mission.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Claude Code does not currently have a SubagentCompleted hook event. The existing events are: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, SessionEnd, SubagentStart, InstructionsLoaded, PermissionRequest, Stop. None fires specifically when a background agent completes. The PreToolUse on Agent (next launch) is the closest available proxy. The Nachbesprechung must therefore be BEHAVIORAL (delegation duty component) rather than STRUCTURAL (hook). Decision #35 says hooks are more effective than behavioral instructions. This is a limitation — acknowledge it and plan for a SubagentCompleted hook when CC supports it.

proposals.what: DO NOT formalize this as a mandatory subagent launch after every mission. The Nachbesprechung must be INLINE — the S3 performs it as part of its own processing, not by launching an S2 analysis agent. Launching a subagent for every mission return would: (a) add ~30s-2min latency per mission (subagent startup, context injection, execution), (b) consume tokens that should go to actual mission work, (c) be overkill for trivial missions (M6 trash check does not need an S2 analyst), (d) conflict with the session's finding that inline synthesis is correct for data already in context (session-aar.json SO-6). The Nachbesprechung is the S3 thinking for 10 seconds, not a governance ceremony.
proposals.why: The commander's question asked 'should a mission analysis SUBAGENT be launched?' The answer is NO — a subagent launch would be disproportionate. The gap is not 'lack of analysis agent' but 'lack of explicit analysis STEP.' The 4 questions are the step. The S3 already has the returned output in context — it just needs to be prompted to analyze it before moving on. This is the difference between PDCA Check (lightweight, inline) and a full AAR (heavyweight, formal).
proposals.barrier_analysis: If the Nachbesprechung is purely behavioral (no subagent, no hook), what prevents the S3 from skipping it? Answer: the same mechanism that enforces any delegation duty component — it is in the prompt, part of the governed protocol, and the commander can observe compliance by checking whether the running estimate was updated at mission boundaries. Non-compliance is detectable: if mission M4 produces 5 proposals but the running estimate was not updated until 3 missions later, the Nachbesprechung was skipped. A future SubagentCompleted hook could inject a reminder.

proposals.what: The term 'Nachbesprechung' (post-discussion/debrief) from German organizational practice. File via /glossary skill with definition: 'A lightweight post-mission check performed inline by the delegating agent when a mission returns. Four questions: (1) assumptions invalidated? (2) Schwerpunkt changed? (3) running estimate update needed? (4) next mission adjustment needed? Distinct from reconciliation (multi-mission synthesis), Lagebeurteilung (periodic full assessment), AAR (formal session-end learning), and S2 consolidation (cross-session intelligence). Produces no formal artifact — updates the running estimate if needed. Intensity scales with mission impact.'
proposals.why: Using a German term continues the provenance pattern established by Schwerpunkt, Lagebeurteilung, Reibung, Mitdenken, and Auftrag. These terms carry precision from their source discipline that English approximations lack. 'Post-mission check' is vague. 'Nachbesprechung' names a specific, lightweight, purpose-built concept.
proposals.barrier_analysis: 6 German terms in the governed vocabulary may be perceived as excessive. But each serves a distinct function: Schwerpunkt (focus), Lagebeurteilung (situation assessment), Reibung (friction), Mitdenken (thinking along), Auftrag (mission-type order), Nachbesprechung (post-mission check). They are not decorative — they name concepts that have no precise English equivalent in the harness context.

doctrinalResearch.question: What does military doctrine say about post-mission analysis?

findings.relevance: Step 2 is Mission Analysis — PRE-plan. There is no post-mission equivalent in MDMP itself. MDMP is a planning process, not an execution process. The post-execution equivalent is the AAR (FM 7-0), which is post-OPERATION, not post-individual-task. MDMP does not govern the BETWEEN of sequential tasks.
findings.conclusion: MDMP does not address the gap. The gap is in execution, not planning.

findings.relevance: After Action Review is conducted after operations, training events, and significant activities. It has 4 questions: What was supposed to happen? What actually happened? Why was there a difference? What can we do differently? AARs are formal, structured, and produce documented lessons. They are NOT lightweight — they are deliberate learning events.
findings.conclusion: AAR is too heavyweight for post-individual-mission. It is the right tool for session-end (decision #36) but not for between-missions.

findings.relevance: In military operations, staff updates happen at FIXED INTERVALS (battle rhythm), not after each individual event. The morning staff update, the evening commander's update brief — these are time-triggered Lagebeurteilungen. Battle update assessments (BUAs) are event-triggered but only by SIGNIFICANT events (contact, major unit movement, logistics crisis). Routine patrol returns do not trigger a BUA.
findings.conclusion: The military model supports TIERED response: routine returns get no analysis, significant returns get a battle update assessment. This maps to the Nachbesprechung scaling heuristic: trivial missions get 10 seconds, impactful missions get minutes.

findings.relevance: The full OODA cycle runs after every action: Observe (mission executes) -> Orient (analyze output, update mental model) -> Decide (determine next action) -> Act (launch next mission). Boyd emphasized that ORIENT is the critical phase — it is where the competitor gains advantage by reorienting faster. Skipping Orient means acting on a stale mental model.
findings.conclusion: OODA explicitly supports the Nachbesprechung. The Orient phase IS the post-mission analysis. Boyd would say skipping it is the primary failure mode.

findings.relevance: CHECK happens after DO. But PDCA Check is lightweight: 'Did the Do produce the expected result?' It is a verification step, not a full re-analysis. Act (the next step) adjusts based on the Check.
findings.conclusion: PDCA supports a lightweight check, not a full analysis. The 4-question Nachbesprechung is closer to PDCA Check than to MDMP Mission Analysis.

findings.relevance: Toyota Kata has 4 steps: (1) Understand the direction, (2) Grasp the current condition, (3) Establish the next target condition, (4) Experiment toward the target. After each experiment, the practitioner returns to step 2 (grasp current condition) before the next experiment. This is explicitly a post-action re-assessment — lightweight, focused on 'what changed?'
findings.conclusion: Toyota Kata directly supports the Nachbesprechung pattern. Step 2 after each experiment IS the post-mission check: 'what is the current condition now that this experiment completed?'

findings.relevance: Sprint retro happens at sprint end, not after each story. But daily standups (what did you do, what will you do, any blockers) ARE a lightweight post-action check. The standup asks: what changed since yesterday? Are there blockers? This is the Nachbesprechung applied to a daily cadence rather than a per-mission cadence.
findings.conclusion: Agile supports periodic lightweight checks (standup) over per-task analysis. But in multi-agent AI, each mission return IS a meaningful boundary — the equivalent of a team member completing a significant piece of work.

doctrinalResearch.synthesis: No doctrine mandates a formal analysis step after every individual subordinate action. But every doctrine includes some form of re-orientation between actions. The question is not WHETHER to re-orient but HOW MUCH: OODA says re-orient every cycle. PDCA says check after every Do. Toyota Kata says re-grasp the current condition after every experiment. Military doctrine says battle update assessment for significant events, nothing for routine. The Nachbesprechung is the right concept: event-triggered, scaled to impact, inline, lightweight. It is OODA Orient + PDCA Check + Kata Step 2, adapted to the multi-agent AI context where 'missions' vary from trivial (check Trash) to architectural (redesign concurrent session model).

shouldItBeFormalized.verdict: YES — as a lightweight delegation duty component, NOT as a mandatory subagent launch
argumentsFor: M16 showed assumptions propagate because post-mission checks are inconsistent — a governed 4-question check would catch assumption invalidation at the earliest possible moment
The running estimate gets stale because updates are ad-hoc — Q3 ('update needed?') forces an update at every significant mission return
M12 found 17 unflagged assumptions — Q1 ('assumptions invalidated?') at each mission return would have surfaced some as they emerged rather than waiting for an end-of-session audit
The commander's ad-hoc interventions (L2040, L2391, L3098) show the NEED exists — the commander was manually performing the Nachbesprechung. Formalizing it means the S3 does it independently
OODA, PDCA, and Toyota Kata all support a post-action re-orientation step as essential, not optional

Decision #35 (structural enforcement over behavioral) applies, but the available structural mechanism (hook) does not exist for this trigger. The delegation duty component is the best available structural approximation.
argumentsAgainst: Adding a mandatory step after every mission slows execution — MITIGATED by scaling heuristic (10 seconds for trivial missions)
For simple missions (M6 trash search), the Nachbesprechung is pure overhead — MITIGATED by scaling heuristic (Q1-Q4 all 'no' in 10 seconds)

The commander's ad-hoc direction is already the mechanism — it works when the commander is present — COUNTERPOINT: it does NOT work when the commander is not present, or when the commander misses a significant return (M4's concurrent session finding was not connected to earlier missions for several turns)

Decision #35 says structural enforcement (hooks) over behavioral (instructions). The Nachbesprechung is behavioral (no hook exists for mission return) — ACKNOWLEDGED as limitation. Plan for SubagentCompleted hook when CC supports it

The delegation duty is already growing (8 -> 9 -> proposed 13 components). Adding component 14 increases complexity — MITIGATED by temporal separation: components 1-12 fire at launch, component 13 fires at return. The S3 does not hold all 14 in mind simultaneously
shouldItBeFormalized.recommendation: Formalize the Nachbesprechung as delegation duty component 13 (or next available number). Define it as the 4-question lightweight check. Include the scaling heuristic. Do NOT make it a subagent launch. Do NOT make it a full Lagebeurteilung. It is the ORIENT phase of the delegation OODA loop — the minimal step that keeps the S3's mental model current between missions.

isThisMDMPStep2Applied.question: Is this just MDMP Step 2 applied post-mission, or something new?
isThisMDMPStep2Applied.answer: It is something NEW — it is OODA Orient applied to multi-agent operations, not MDMP Step 2 applied recursively.
isThisMDMPStep2Applied.reasoning: MDMP Step 2 (Mission Analysis) enumerates facts, assumptions, constraints, and tasks BEFORE writing a plan. It is a comprehensive, formal, documented process that produces a planning brief. Applying it post-mission would mean: re-enumerate all facts (overkill after a single mission), re-check all assumptions (the full set, not just the ones this mission might have affected), re-assess all constraints (most unchanged). This would be a full Lagebeurteilung, not a lightweight check. The Nachbesprechung is lighter than MDMP Step 2: it asks 4 targeted questions scoped to what THIS mission changed. It is closer to OODA Orient (update mental model) or PDCA Check (did it work?) than to MDMP Step 2 (enumerate everything).

conceptualMap.MDMPStep2: Pre-plan, comprehensive, formal, produces planning brief. Governed by decision #13.
conceptualMap.Lagebeurteilung: Periodic, comprehensive, mandatory categories, even if nothing changed. Governed by /handoff skill, proposed Stop hook.
conceptualMap.Nachbesprechung: Per-mission, scoped to what changed, 4 questions, inline, no formal output. Proposed as delegation duty component.
conceptualMap.Reconciliation: Per-batch, synthesizes multiple parallel outputs, produces ranked proposals. Proposed in M14.
conceptualMap.AAR: Per-session/plan, formal structured learning, produces documented lessons. Governed by decision #36.
conceptualMap.S2Consolidation: Per-plan, S2 reads all findings and produces intelligence brief. Governed by decision #26.

The framework registry was re-read. 'Mission command' is proposed, not yet adopted. The Nachbesprechung would be part of Mission Command (delegation lifecycle). No framework covers the post-mission gap today.
